findings: The first SDK list is moved into shared_ptr<const List>; returned borrowed Views copy shared ownership, not champion handles.
The list has no public mutable access or mutable alias. Live entity methods are still SDK reads.
A temporary View returned to range-for remains alive for the entire loop; begin/end both refer to one owned immutable list.
Outstanding Views retain the list after scope destruction, invalidation or replacement; no dangling iterator/reference is created by those events.
The uncached fallback owns its fresh vector by move, so it is also safe to iterate.
Ancestor invalidation and no-recache policy remain intact; invalidation affects future queries, not the lifetime of already acquired ranges.
The eight selected caller loops perform no actions while iterating; their mutation ordering is unchanged.
Nested scopes are lexical and nonmovable; restoring the active parent pointer is safe in the actual single-scope production use.
limits: Old acquired handle lists do not magically become new visibility lists after an action; current callers deliberately finish these loops before acting.
New future action-inside-loop callsites require another review.
This is a source lifetime audit, not native fuel or playing-strength proof.
